statutes.act: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985

facts: The appellant is a judicial officer in the State of Uttar Pradesh.
He joined the Provincial Civil Service (Judicial) in the year 1976 and in May 1994 he was promoted to the Higher Judicial Service and posted as Addl. District & Sessions Judge at Jhansi.
A crime No. 180 of 1995 registered by the Police Station at Nawabad was committed to the Sessions Court at Jhansi and allotted to the appellant's court for trial and disposal.
The crime related to an incident which happened on 22.5.1995.

The allegation in the First Information Report was that accused Ram Pal and Raghunath used fire-arms and shot dead Pratap Yadubir Singh and Devendra Pipraiya within the compound of District Panchayat Bhawan at Jhansi.
issues: Whether the bail order passed by the appellant was for extraneous consideration with oblique motive on insufficient grounds
Whether the appellant received illegal gratification for granting bail
petitioner_arguments: The charge, if at all, was vague and it only stated that the bail order had been passed by the delinquent officer [appellant] for extraneous consideration with oblique motive on insufficient grounds, without cogent and tangible reasons
There was no specific charge that the appellant received any monetary consideration from any of the accused or his relatives
respondent_arguments: The bail had been granted by the appellant in utter disregard of judicial norms and on insufficient grounds and based on extraneous consideration with oblique motive
court_reasoning: The Judge who conducted the inquiry elaborately considered the various aspects of the matter and concluded that there was no element of truth in the allegation that the appellant had received illegal gratification

However, the learned Judge inquiring the matter eventually came to the conclusion that the bail had been granted by the appellant in utter disregard of judicial norms and on insufficient grounds and based on extraneous consideration with oblique motive
holding: The Full Court by its resolution imposed a major punishment of withholding two annual increments of the appellant with cumulative effect
The Division Bench reduced the appellant to the rank next below, that is, Civil Judge (Senior Division)
